identity.title: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
identity.abstract: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual–inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. We present Accord, which constructs an accurate online dense metric map from any camera with an IMU. A VIO filter publishes metric poses, a depth foundation model conditioned on them predicts depth for short keyframe windows, and a factor graph fuses the resulting submaps. Recent work has explored several approaches to this problem. What is essential is the multi-view agreement (Accord), which is considered in SLAM as a source of geometric self-consistency. Accord anchors each keyframe window to metric 3D points triangulated from the filter poses, then exploits bidirectional dense depth agreement between co-visible images to estimate and correct per-image scale errors while preserving the metric scale established by the anchors. Context keyframes further improve depth prediction, and the resulting submaps are fused in a factor graph. We evaluate a single mapping configuration across five public camera–IMU setups and a new Phone-rig/GoPro dataset. With nothing tuned per dataset/setup and every map aligned only by Accord's own trajectory, Accord achieves consistently best/second-best mean F-score at 5 cm on every platform. Accord is open-source along with the phone-rig dataset for the benefit of the research community.

note: What the page shows and where it comes from. Paths are under build_site.py's --source. A map with a report is placed by the report's map_to_reference (the rigid fit of its trajectory to the reference trajectory, nothing fitted to the scan) and must be the cloud the report scored (SHA-256); points are other pipelines' scored clouds, already placed by their reports. Accord's: of a sequence's runs of record, the one of the median map score, DA3-Giant. Phone rig: Accord's run of a recording is, of its three, the one of the median map score at 5 cm; beside it the reference's own map (RTAB-Map on a LiDAR iPhone), as the release ships it.

spectrum.alt: Every dense pipeline's map F-score at 5 cm on every scanned sequence of EuRoC, ORI, Hilti-Oxford and Oxford Spires
spectrum.caption: Every scanned sequence. The map's F-score at 5 cm per sequence, each placed by its system's own trajectory; the means are the table's. An × at 0: no map, or the map of a trajectory that failed (more than 10 m off). † given the reference's scale; ‡ the mapper alone, on Accord's poses.

spires.alt: Accord and FoundationVIO on Oxford Spires CC05: the scan each covers, and a slice of both maps coloured by distance to the scan
spires.caption: Accord against FoundationVIO outdoors (Oxford Spires CC05, the sequence where Accord is furthest ahead). (a) The scan the reference cameras saw, from above, blue where the map comes within 5 cm of it, with each system's own trajectory. (b) The scene cut 1.5 m above the ground, 10 cm thick, around the 20 m square where both maps have the most points in the slice: the scan in grey, each map point coloured by its distance to the scan. Both maps placed by their own trajectories; Accord's: the median of three runs.

results.title: Public benchmarks
results.note: The paper's Tab. 2, as typeset. Means over each dataset's sequences. Maps: the F-score at 5 cm, each placed by its system's own trajectory (Hilti-Oxford: the three sequences its scan covers). Trajectories: the error in cm (Hilti-Oxford: at the surveyed points where the reference is sparse). ×: every sequence failed (no output, or a trajectory more than 10 m off). –: not run, or no trajectory of its own. † given the reference's scale. ‡ with its own depth model, on Accord's poses. Bold: the best; underlined: the second best.

results.title: Phone rig
results.note: The paper's Tab. 3, as typeset. Means over each phone's recordings: the map's F-score at 5 and 10 cm against the LiDAR phone's map, placed by the system's own trajectory, and the trajectory's error in m after a rigid fit. ×: failed. –: not run, or no trajectory of its own. † given the reference's scale. ‡ with its own depth model, on Accord's poses. Bold: the best; underlined: the second best.
